chunks: For each We have appointed heirs to what parents and relatives leave behind. And to those you have given your pledge in marriage give their share, for God is witness to everything.

key_terms.عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ: those with whom you made a covenant/pledge (often referring to spouses or allies)
key_terms.مَوَالِيَ: heirs or those entitled to inheritance

ai.seo_question: Who are the designated heirs for inheritance according to this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited alongside 4:11-12, clarifies the scope of inheritance by including 'mawali' (allies or freedmen) alongside parents and close relatives, reflecting the pre-Islamic and early Islamic social structure of patronage. It underscores the divine precision in allocating shares, with God as the ultimate witness to ensure justice in the distribution of the deceased's estate.
